title: Fragile SQL column prefix in list_audio_channels
description:
In fieldwork-db/src/audio_db.rs line 328, the list_audio_channels query builds column aliases via CHANNEL_COLS.replace(", ", ", ac."). This only prefixes columns after the first comma -- the first column 'persona_id' is NOT prefixed with 'ac.'. The resulting SELECT is 'SELECT ac.persona_id, ac.description, ...' only because the string actually starts with 'persona_id' which gets 'ac.' from the format string 'SELECT ac.{}'.

Actually, re-reading the code: format!("SELECT ac.{}", CHANNEL_COLS.replace(", ", ", ac.")) does prefix the first column via the format string. So the output is correct. However, the replace approach is fragile: if any column name appears as a substring of another or if CHANNEL_COLS formatting changes (e.g. spaces around commas change), the SQL silently breaks. This is a code smell, not a bug.

Location: /home/mark/PROJECT/fedistract/fieldwork-db/src/audio_db.rs:324-329
close_reason: Accepted risk: the string-replace column aliasing is fragile but correct today. ponytail-level concern — would fix if adding new columns to audio_channels.
